synthetic.name: Mining (Lithium, Nickel, Cobalt, Graphite)
synthetic.notes: Geologically concentrated but geographically spread across Australia, Chile, and China (lithium), the Democratic Republic of Congo (cobalt), Indonesia (nickel), and China (graphite). Medium transparency: national mining statistics are public, but artisanal cobalt mining in the DRC carries documented governance and labor opacity.
synthetic.data_quality: Medium: national mining statistics public; artisanal cobalt mining governance and labor conditions opaque

synthetic.name: Mineral Refining and Processing
synthetic.notes: BOTTLENECK, worst phase in the chain. China refines approximately 65% of global lithium, roughly 75% of global cobalt, and over 90% of global graphite. This is an extreme midstream chokepoint exposed to export licensing and trade-policy risk, including proposed and in some cases implemented Chinese export restrictions on battery cathode and lithium/graphite processing technology. Low-medium transparency at the refinery ownership and contract level.
synthetic.data_quality: Low-medium: refinery ownership and long-term supply contracts rarely disclosed publicly

metrics.export_control_risk: Documented and ongoing policy risk on battery cathode and lithium/graphite processing technology

synthetic.name: Cathode and Anode Material Production
synthetic.notes: Second bottleneck. China holds approximately 85% of global cathode active material (CAM) production capacity (including NMC and LFP chemistries) and over 90% (some sources cite up to 98%) of anode active material (AAM) production capacity, predominantly graphite-based. Low-medium transparency: material specifications are proprietary and supply contracts are rarely disclosed.
synthetic.data_quality: Low-medium: cathode/anode material specifications proprietary; supply contracts rarely disclosed

synthetic.name: Cell Manufacturing
synthetic.notes: China produces roughly 75-76% of global lithium-ion cell output (up from 57% in 2021 and 68% in 2022), with CATL and BYD dominant. The United States, EU, Korea, and Japan hold growing capacity (LGES, Samsung SDI, Panasonic as counterweights). Global battery production reached roughly 3 TWh of capacity in 2024. Chinese battery prices fell nearly 30% in 2024, roughly 30% cheaper than European and 20% cheaper than North American equivalents. Medium-high transparency: cell shipment volumes are tracked by BloombergNEF and national industry associations.
synthetic.data_quality: Medium-high: cell shipment volumes tracked by BloombergNEF and national industry associations

metrics.dominant_manufacturers: CATL, BYD (China); LGES, Samsung SDI (Korea); Panasonic (Japan)

synthetic.name: Pack Assembly and Deployment (EV and Grid Storage)
synthetic.notes: Battery packs are integrated into EVs and grid-scale storage systems, the structural link between transport decarbonization and grid storage that this project is designed to surface. High transparency: EV sales and grid storage deployment are tracked nationally via the IEA Global EV Outlook.
synthetic.data_quality: High: EV sales and grid storage deployment tracked nationally (IEA Global EV Outlook)

metrics.deployment_pathways: EV traction packs; stationary grid-scale storage
metrics.structural_role: Links transport decarbonization demand to grid storage capacity growth

synthetic.name: Second-Life and Recycling
synthetic.notes: Nascent recycling infrastructure. Under 5% of retired EV battery packs are formally recycled at scale as of the mid-2020s (PROVISIONAL estimate, industry reporting), since large-volume first-generation EV battery retirements have not yet arrived at scale. Low transparency: end-of-life battery flows and second-life repurposing volumes are poorly tracked globally.
synthetic.data_quality: Low: end-of-life battery flows and second-life repurposing volumes poorly tracked globally

metrics.note: Large-volume first-generation EV battery retirements not yet at scale as of mid-2020s

system.interpretation: The lithium battery supply chain scores 81.5% average balance (Good zone). Phase 1 (Mineral Refining and Processing) is the structural bottleneck at 67.2% (Fair), the most concentrated and export-control-exposed stage in the chain: China refines approximately 65% of global lithium, 75% of global cobalt, and over 90% of global graphite. Phase 2 (Cathode and Anode Material Production) is the second-weakest phase at 72.9% (Fair), reflecting China's approximately 85% share of cathode and over 90% share of anode active material capacity. Both phases carry high D (constraint load from geographic concentration and proprietary contracting) relative to C (globally diversified contribution capacity). Phase 4 (Pack Assembly and Deployment) is the strongest phase at 87.0%, reflecting the structural link between transport decarbonization and grid storage that is tracked with high transparency via national EV sales statistics. Phase 5 (Second-Life and Recycling) remains structurally weak (78.4%) due to nascent circular economy infrastructure, with under 5% of retired EV battery packs formally recycled at scale as of the mid-2020s (PROVISIONAL).

baseline.notes: pi = chain average balance across 6 phases (Good zone). phi = proportional value distribution: upstream mining countries (Chile, DRC, Indonesia, Australia) capture a small share of chain value relative to midstream refining and material processing concentrated in China, a resource-curse-pattern phi failure; Stressed zone, just above the 61.8 Failure boundary. sqrt2 = structural overhead: export licensing risk and critical-minerals trade-policy exposure are documented structural friction on the refining and materials stages; Stressed zone. ln2 = growth/transformation: battery cell costs have fallen roughly 30% year over year in China per IEA/SMM reporting, a strong value-transformation track record; Stressed-to-Coherent boundary. e = financial abstraction: critical minerals funds, US IRA battery production credits (45X), and Defense Production Act Title III funding exist but are not yet fully linked to measurable supply-chain diversification KPIs; Stressed zone.
